Use this as the handoff prompt for a new chat:

KORELUMINA RECONSTRUCTION RULES
We are performing regression reconstruction, not greenfield development.
Many features already existed in previous commits, branches, tags, or stashes. The objective is to recover known-working implementations, not invent new ones.
Core Rule
Before writing new code:


Identify the regression.


Find where it last worked.


Recover from:


current branch history


recovery branches


tags


stashes


known green commits




Compare implementations.


Restore the smallest proven-good change.


Never redesign a subsystem that already existed.

RECONSTRUCTION SEARCH ORDER
For every regression:
Step 1
Confirm current state.
Examples:
Bashgit rev-parse --short HEAD
git status
Step 2
Identify affected module.
Examples:


Runtime


Preview


Dashboard


Workspace


Project selection


File tree


Runtime toolbar


Step 3
Search recovery sources.
Order:


current branch history


recovery branch


stash@{0}


stash@{1}


stash@{2}


stash@{3}


known green tags


older stable branches


Step 4
Diff working vs broken.
Examples:
Bashgit diff GOOD_COMMIT..HEAD -- path/to/file
Bashgit show stash@{3}:path/to/file
Step 5
Restore only the missing behavior.
Avoid unrelated changes.

ISSUE INVESTIGATION RULE
Always prove the failure.
Examples:
Runtime
Bashcurl http://localhost:4100/health
Bashcurl "http://localhost:4100/api/runtime/status?projectId=elegance-sync-app"
Bashcurl -X POST http://localhost:4100/api/runtime/start \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"projectId":"elegance-sync-app"}'
Browser
JavaScriptdocument.querySelectorAll("iframe").length
JavaScript[...document.querySelectorAll("iframe")].map(x => ({
  src: x.src,
  width: x.clientWidth,
  height: x.clientHeight
}))
Never assume.
Verify.

ONE ISSUE AT A TIME
Do not fix multiple regressions simultaneously.
Workflow:


identify issue


recover implementation


verify


commit


push


move to next issue



COMMIT GUARDRAIL
After a fix is verified:
Create recovery branch
Bashgit checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b fix/<module>-<issue>
Commit
Bashgit add .
git commit -m "fix(module): restore <behavior>"
Push
Use:
Bashkpush "fix(module): restore <behavior>"
Never force push.
Never commit to main.

REQUIRED VERIFICATION BEFORE COMMIT
For runtime/preview issues:


Runtime health OK


Runtime start works


Runtime status works


activeProject populated


runtimeUrl populated


iframe exists


Preview renders


No runtime errors


No console errors related to fix


Examples:
JavaScriptactiveProject
JavaScriptruntimeUrl
JavaScriptdocument.querySelectorAll("iframe").length

AFTER FIXING AN ISSUE
Immediately:


Verify behavior.


Commit only the fix.


Push with kpush.


Record:


issue fixed


commit hash


branch name




Return to clean state.


Begin investigation of next regression.


Never stack multiple unverified fixes into a single commit.

Yes. That is the cleaner move now.
What you’re doing has crossed the point where archaeology costs more than rebuilding the wiring cleanly. Use the current repo as a reference museum, not the working tree.
Recommended path:
1. Freeze current repo exactly as-is
2. Fresh clone clean repo
3. Create one reconstruction branch
4. Re-wire only proven modules from the old repo/stashes
5. Verify each subsystem before moving on
Do this first in the current repo:
Bashcd ~/dev/korelumina

git status

git stash push -u -m "FULL-SNAPSHOT-before-fresh-clone-restart"

git tag reconstruction-abandoned-archaeology-snapshot

git branch backup/reconstruction-abandoned-archaeology
Then fresh clone:
Bashcd ~/dev

git clone git@github.com:kore20lllc-netizen/korelumina.git korelumina-clean

cd korelumina-clean

git checkout -b feature/clean-master-os-wiring
npm install
Use the old repo only as reference:
Old repo:
~/dev/korelumina

Fresh repo:
~/dev/korelumina-clean
Clean wiring order:
1. Project dashboard / activeProject
2. Runtime service client
3. Root dev supervisor
4. useRuntimeBoot
5. PreviewFrame
6. RuntimeToolbar
7. DeveloperWorkspace Monaco + filetree
8. Save/read/write runtime FS
9. Commit green checkpoint
Rule for the fresh clone:
No stash apply.
No bulk cherry-pick.
No full subsystem overwrite unless verified.
Only copy exact files or exact blocks after comparing.
This is the right call. Keep the old repo untouched as evidence/reference; make the fresh clone the new clean reconstruction workspace.
